drhp.business: Technology platform company operating across two interlinked layers: digital connectivity (provided through subsidiary RJIL, the licensed telecom entity) and digital products & services sold to consumers and enterprises. Revenue comes from wireless and fixed broadband subscriptions, enterprise managed services, and digital product monetisation. RJIL holds the licensed spectrum and connectivity assets; JPL holds the IP and applications layer. April–March fiscal year.
drhp.one_liner: Jio Platforms Limited operates India's pan-India digital connectivity network and a portfolio of consumer and enterprise digital services, built on proprietary end-to-end technology across 5G, fiber, and applications.

other_material_facts.value: India’s nominal GDP grew at an 11.77% CAGR in FY2021-2026 as shown in Figure 2 An exchange rate of US$1 = ₹90 has been used across the report for presentation purposes, unless stated otherwise.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: This translates into an expected nominal GDP CAGR of 10.82% during FY2026-31.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: As illustrated in Figure 3.5, the current ARPU forecast remains below the level implied by this global relationship. 36 FY2019 ARPU corresponds to 2018 calendar year data ARPU for MBB customers, estimated based on data traffic of MBB customers and price per GB Figure 3.5: Global benchmarks for mobile ARPU [Source: GSMA Intelligence, IMF.WEO.202637, 2025] Key growth drivers Wider availability of good quality 4G and 5G networks Over the past few years, digital connectivity providers have made significant investments in expanding and upgrading 4G and 5G infrastructure, both to improve coverage and to enhance network capacity.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: With increasing infrastructure availability and improving household affordability, fixed broadband penetration is likely to accelerate, with customers projected to increase to 150.4 million at a 18.90% CAGR over Q1 FY2027-FY2031.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: As digital connectivity providers overcome these barriers around limited network availability through roll-out of next-generation technologies like FWA on 5G and UBR, the market has the potential to move quickly to unlock the latent demand for reliable, high-speed digital connectivity 47 As per TeleGeography Figure 4.3: Global benchmarks for fixed broadband penetration48, FY2026 [Source: TRAI TSD, Government reports, TeleGeography] Market size The fixed broadband market in India is projected to increase from ₹340-350 billion (~US$4 billion) in FY2026 to ₹920-930 billion (~US$10 billion) by FY2031.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Key growth drivers This next phase of India’s fixed broadband growth will be underpinned by four key structural drivers: Expanding affordability and addressable market due to increasing income Increasing affordability is expected to be a key driver of fixed broadband adoption among Indian households.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Based on prevailing market trends and the scope of Jio’s current consumer offerings, the overall opportunity can be assessed across four high-growth digital services verticals: Digital entertainment The digital entertainment segment is set to grow from ₹562 billion (~US$6.2 billion) in FY2026 to ₹920 billion (~US$10.2 billion) by FY2031 at a 10% CAGR, driven by accelerated OTT, audio-streaming and cloud-gaming adoption In India, the digital entertainment segment comprises OTT video services, pay TV, audio streaming and cloud gaming.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Personal digital productivity solutions The personal digital productivity solutions segment is expected to grow from ₹160 billion (US$1.8 billion) in FY2026 to ₹482 billion (US$5.4 billion) in FY2031 at a 25% CAGR, driven by adoption of productivity tools and cloud These solutions constitute the digital architecture that helps consumers to work across devices, store their personal content, and increasingly rely on intelligent assistance in everyday tasks.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: The overall market is expected to grow at a 25% CAGR (FY2026- 2031).

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Smart-home IoT The smart-home IoT segment is expected to grow from ₹96 billion (US$1.1 billion) in FY2026 to ₹322 billion (US$3.6 billion) in FY2031 at a 27% CAGR, driven by increasing adoption of end-to-end smart-home stack, offering affordable yet interoperable device options The smart-home IoT segment comprises connected devices and platforms that enable consumers to automate, monitor and control their home environment through a unified interface.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Figure 5.2: Overview of enterprise digital services market dynamics and Jio addressable market size, FY2026 Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) as a growth driver In India, enterprise digital adoption is accelerating rapidly across all business sizes, gradually converging on deep digital transformation goals: Large enterprises: These have historically led enterprise digital adoption and currently exhibit high penetration across core enterprise digital services, estimated at approximately 75 to 90%.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: While hardware and managed services will remain foundational components of the enterprise digital services market size, their relative share is expected to decline as organisations prioritise software-led, cloud-based and service-driven models.

overview.business_overview:
We are a technology platform, built on proprietary digital technology and pan-India digital connectivity as the foundational layer, driving digital transformation in India. Since our inception, we have played a pivotal role in democratising access to digital connectivity and digital services in India. Jio Platforms’ digital connectivity forms one of the fundamental pillars of India’s growing digital economy, which is expected to reach $1.4 trillion (₹125.8 trillion) by Fiscal 2031, as per the Analysys Mason Report. Our Subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited (“RJIL”), served 533.3 million customers in India, as of June 30, 2026. A combination of mobile, fixed broadband and digital services across a unified platform, together with data and customer personalisation, positions us as a comprehensive digital gateway for accessing the internet, digital services and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (“AI”).

For more details on each of our strengths, see “ – Our Strengths” on page 206.

Our business model is built on a proprietary technology stack that we have designed, developed and deployed in-house. We have vertically integrated technology capabilities across network, device engineering, software and operating systems, and digital applications. This full-stack ownership helps us to significantly reduce dependency on third-party vendors, provides structural cost advantages, and enables faster innovation cycles. As of June 30, 2026, our Company had 12,477 employees in the digital products and technology development team, representing approximately 45% of our total full-time employees. As of June 30, 2026, the Company and its Subsidiaries have applied for 7,220 patents, across 4G, 5G, 6G cloud-native core network architectures, AI-driven network automation, and other digital technologies within India and outside India. The Company was ranked among the top 20 global companies in the Patent Cooperation Treaty rankings in 2025, according to the World Intellectual Property Organisation. We believe this depth of proprietary technology provides us with a competitive advantage and positions us as a technology platform that uses connectivity as its foundational core distribution layer. Further, by leveraging this proprietary technology stack, we are transitioning into an AI-native digital services company endeavouring to deliver connected intelligence and agentic AI services at scale to consumers and businesses.

Our Technology Platform

In modern software-driven network architecture, the traditional distinction between ‘telecom’ and ‘technology’ no longer applies. Our position is more grounded in technology, given that we have designed, built, and deployed our entire network and services stack primarily using proprietary technology, from radio access network to core capabilities, from operating systems to digital applications. Technology is the fundamental architecture of how our business is structured, built, and operated.

In this context:

• Our Company had 12,477 full-time employees in digital products and technology development as of June 30, 2026, representing approximately 45% of our total full-time employees. Of these 12,477 employees, 8,156 are involved in the development of digital products and services while the remaining are engaged in network technology engineering;

• We have filed 7,220 patent applications across 4G, 5G, 6G cloud-native core network architectures, AI-driven network automation, and digital technologies - with 2,655 applications in India and 4,565 filed across foreign jurisdictions, as of June 30, 2026. We are the only Indian company to be among the top 20 companies globally in the WIPO Patent Cooperation Treaty (“PCT”) rankings in 2025 - a distinction that places us alongside leading global technology firms70;

• We are the only digital connectivity provider globally with an end-to-end, proprietary 5G standalone (“SA”) technology stack, as per the Analysys Mason Report;

• We have in-house hardware and software capabilities - evidenced through the design of our set-top-box and the JioBharat OS, which can operate on low-cost chipsets and with minimal memory footprint, enabling high quality digital services on affordable devices;

• JioBrain, our proprietary AI engine, is embedded across network operations enabling autonomous decision making for capacity allocation, fault prediction, and real-time network optimisation;

• JioAirFiber scaled to 14.0 million customers as of June 30, 2026, from the time of its launch in September 2023 – making it the largest fixed wireless customer base in India – enabled by our proprietary UBR-based fixed wireless access (“FWA”) technology, as per the Analysys Mason Report;

• We have pioneered successive technology waves in India: - in 4G, we were the first to roll out an all-IP, greenfield 4G LTE network at scale and achieved 100 million

in 5G, we achieved the fastest rollout globally with pan-India coverage in 15 months and 284.9 million customers in 45 months as per the Analysys Mason Report. 70 World Intellectual Property Organization (2026). A Comprehensive portfolio of offerings75

Our offerings encompass various aspects of modern digital society, as described below:

We offer consumers:

• Digital Connectivity (4G, 5G, JioFiber, JioAirFiber): Mobile and fixed broadband services provided by RJIL to subscribers as per their connectivity plans;

• Digital Entertainment (JioTV+, JioSaavn, JioGames, JioHotstar): Video/music streaming and cloud gaming provided by the Company, RJIL and Saavn Media Limited bundled with connectivity plans;

• Cloud and Productivity (JioAICloud, JioPC): Cloud storage and virtual PC services provided by the Company to subscribers on bundled or standalone basis;

• Smart Home and IoT (Jio Set-top-box, JioHome): Connected devices enabling home automation. “IoT” (Internet of Things) refers to a network of connected devices and sensors that collect, exchange and act on data with minimal human intervention. Provided by the Company and RJIL on device sale or

• AI Products (JioBrain, Google AI Pro): AI assistants and personalised digital experiences provided by the Company and Jio Haptik Technologies Limited in partnership with third parties and offered as bundled with the connectivity plans.

We offer businesses:

• Enterprise Connectivity (JioBusiness, Internet Leased Line (“ILL”)76, MPLS77, VPN78): Broadband and leased line connectivity provided by RJIL on a contract-based subscription model;

• Enterprise IoT (JioThings, CPaaS): IoT solutions, or “internet of things” solutions for smart metering, fleet management and industrial monitoring provided by Jio Things Limited and RJIL on device sale or subscription basis;

• Cloud and Security (Managed Wi-Fi, Private 5G, Software-Defined Wide Area Network (“SD- WAN”)79): Enterprise cloud, Wi-Fi, and security solutions provided by the Company and RJIL in partnership with Microsoft and Google Cloud on subscription basis;

• Managed Services (Managed Network Operations Centre (“NoC”), unified communications): End-to-end managed information and communication services provided by the Company under contracts; and

• Enterprise AI (JioBrain): AI enterprise suite for forecasting, automation and network optimisation provided by the Company on subscription/ usage basis. 75  The Company operates as a single operating segment. Except for digital connectivity (which constitutes substantially all revenue), standalone revenue contributions for individual products are not separately disclosed as they are bundled with or subsumed within connectivity services.

A market leader in digital connectivity services

We have been at the forefront of digital adoption in India by making access to digital services ubiquitous through our digital connectivity network. Since our launch in 2016, we fundamentally reshaped digital connectivity for India, and created an all-internet protocol-led 4G network for consumers to seamlessly access digital services. In Fiscal 2026, ~60% of India’s wireless data traffic was on our network, and as of June 30, 2026, we were the largest digital connectivity player with ~1.4 times the 4G+5G subscribers compared to the second largest player in India. Further, our digital connectivity network carried the second highest mobile data globally, in Fiscal 2026. (Source:

As shown in the image below, we played a pivotal role in transitioning India from a data scarce nation to a data abundant nation:

Staying ahead of the technology curve and innovation since launch We launched our 4G network with 4G voice over LTE (“VoLTE”) technology in 2016 and were amongst the first few greenfield all-internet protocol operators globally to launch 4G voice on this technology. India is one of the fastest adopters of 5G globally and we are the first operator in India to launch a standalone 5G network, with 284.9 million 5G subscribers as of June 30, 2026. We launched our 5G offering in October 2022, and achieved a record rollout, deploying more than one million 5G cells within one year. As of March 31, 2026, our 5G customer base was the third largest in the world. (Source: Analysys Mason Report) To support the 5G rollout, we developed a “Made in India”, end-to-end 5G technology stack with our own portfolio of 4G+5G combination core, 5G devices and our OSS and BSS operating systems, as per the Analysys Mason Report. Built on a modern, software-defined architecture with extensive automation and in-house orchestration platforms, this stack supports rapid design, testing and nationwide rollout at scale. With this capability, we helped India become only the fifth country globally to possess such indigenous 5G capability, as per the Analysys Mason Report.

Our key competitive strengths in the global technology landscape with respect to our principal business of digital connectivity and services are summarised below:

• End-to-end ownership of 5G technology stack: We developed a ‘Made in India’ end-to-end 5G technology stack with our own portfolio of 4G+5G combination core, 5G devices and our OSS and BSS operating systems - making us one of the very few connectivity providers globally with such a stack deployed at nationwide scale, as per the Analysys Mason Report.

• Proprietary UBR technology: We have developed a proprietary point-to-point unlicensed band radio (UBR) technology and are the first company in India to offer fixed wireless access services through UBR technology, as per the Analysys Mason Report. We believe UBR technology gives us strategic advantage for faster and more cost-efficient customer acquisition across India and opens opportunities for customer acquisition globally.

• Device and Software Engineering: We have in-house integrated hardware and software design capabilities to launch devices of different form-factors at compelling price-performance ratio. For example: JioBharat phone is an example of our device engineering capabilities, and integration with network technology and operating systems and application capabilities.

• Multiple digital applications for digital use-cases: We have created multiple applications, including MyJioApp, JioTV+, JioSaavn, JioAICloud and JioGames. We had 362.6 million average monthly active users (“MAU”) across our family of applications80 for the three months ended June 30, 2026. For businesses, we offer solutions such as Managed Wi-fi and hybrid cloud.

• AI and AI-led technology systems in our network operations: We have developed automation in managing our network operations and performance, which includes cell tower network that runs on automatic, remote antenna tilt optimisation, “JioBrain” for delivering predictive insights and real-time anomaly detection for proactive network health monitoring, churn detection, spam detection, anomaly forecasting, and dynamic dashboards.

A highly engaged and diversified customer base

The growth of our digital connectivity and digital service offerings has strengthened our market leadership in India, as demonstrated below:

Our digital connectivity reach extended to more than 99% of India’s population for wireless broadband, as of June 30, 2026. We have a multi-layered phygital network for providing access of own and third-party digital services, including:

• Jio Set-top-box and JioTV+ application to enable at home digital use cases across entertainment, cloud compute, cloud gaming and smart home solutions; and • A pan-India network of localised and scalable physical touchpoints with feet-on-street personnel trained for direct sales, at-home installation and handling customer queries.

Our consumer base is diversified across demographics, income brackets and geographic locations. For example:

• Approximately 43% of our mobility customers fell within the digitally proficient age demographic of 18 to 35 years, as of June 30, 2026;

• we had 284.9 million 5G consumers on our network as of June 30, 2026, which represented a premium consumer base with a propensity to adopt new digital services products faster;

• approximately 64% and 36% of fixed broadband customer additions for the three months ended June 30, 2026, were added to our network from urban and rural areas, respectively.

We are a preferred “Gateway to Digital India”

Our pan-India reach and highly engaged customer base of 533.3 million customers as of June 30, 2026, and multi-layered access ecosystem make us a preferred “Gateway to Digital India”, as per the Analysys Mason Report. For example, Jio Financial Services Limited’s JioFinance application is available to our large customer base through the MyJio App. Further, during sporting events like the Indian Premier League 2026 (“IPL 2026”), over 198.7 million viewers accessed the IPL 2026 content through an integrated JioHotstar package with our connectivity services.

In partnership with Reliance Intelligence Limited, we provide access to the Google AI Pro plan to Jio Unlimited 5G users at no extra cost for 18 months. We also intend to distribute enterprise AI products of Reliance Enterprise Intelligence Limited, a joint venture between Reliance Intelligence Limited and a subsidiary of Meta Platforms Inc., to businesses in India.

Our digital gateway capability creates a moat that would be difficult to replicate: one platform surface across mobile, home and enterprise, through which consumers and businesses have access to personalised products across multiple digital categories (connectivity, compute, content, financial services and AI). Our next-gen technology, large scale operations and distribution network, drive customer demand for our offerings, enabling us to offer a compelling price performance proposition. Each additional service distributed through our platform adds revenue at low incremental acquisition cost, deepens and strengthens our customer engagement.

Multiple self-reinforcing flywheels

Our technology platform powers multiple self-reinforcing flywheels, underpinned by AI and machine learning capabilities embedded across our operations. These flywheels have helped us deepen customer engagement, enhance monetisation and strengthen our partner ecosystem, driving scalable and capital-efficient growth. Our AI capabilities draw on large volumes of customer data that create a self-reinforcing flywheel of higher engagement, generating more customer insights, which in turn allows us to enhance customer experience.

• Technology Flywheel: As our platform scales, we are able to enhance the monetisation of our digital connectivity and digital services. Improved monetisation enables more investments in our technological capabilities across network, device, operating systems and digital applications, enabling the development

• Data Flywheel: As of June 30, 2026, RJIL had 533.3 million customers. The average usage of data per month was 43.7 GB per customer in the quarter ended June 30, 2026. High engagement generates better customer insights that help us design better products for varied use cases for our consumers. We can effectively integrate digital services with our digital connectivity subscription plans and launch new products and services based on the engagement of our customers on our network. As our suite of products and services increases, we can attract more customers to our platform.

• Distribution Flywheel: Our pan-India reach, large and highly engaged customer base, together with multi-layered access ecosystem, make us a preferred gateway to digital India, as per the Analysys Mason Report. This value proposition makes our platform attractive for Indian and global partners to work with us to distribute their digital services in India. Such partnerships further increase the suite of products and services we can offer to our customers, further attracting more customers to our platform.

Promoter pedigree and group synergies

Reliance Industries Limited, the Promoter, is India’s largest private sector company by market capitalisation as of June 30, 2026, as per the Analysys Mason Report. Reliance Group has access to and understanding of Indian consumers through its extensive offerings across retail, media, and entertainment and consumer products. We leverage this reach to enable access to our own- and third-party digital services. For example, RJIL has a master distribution agreement with Reliance Retail Limited for distribution of telecommunication services across its pan- India retail network. In addition, we have created a media technology platform, which is also used by JioHotstar (the media and entertainment platform of the Reliance Group) alongside their in-house technology stack, for providing access to media and entertainment content to their customers.

“Jio” is a strong and trusted brand

“Jio” is a strong and trusted brand with a presence across India, among both consumers and businesses. “Jio” means “to live and to be alive” and has come to symbolise living life to the fullest amongst our customers. Beginning as a brand focused on delivering high-quality digital connectivity, Jio has since evolved into a broader platform of consumer and enterprise offerings, associated with reliability, innovation and value. Because of the success of our business, “Jio” is a household brand in India. “Jio” is now used across various consumer facing offerings, including those of the Promoter’s retail, media and fuel retail offerings - JioMart, AJIO, JioHotstar and Jio-bp. This cross-discipline presence reinforces the “Jio” brand’s salience and strengthens customer loyalty across sectors.

Revenue comes from wireless and fixed broadband subscriptions, enterprise managed services, and digital product monetisation. RJIL holds the licensed spectrum and connectivity assets; JPL holds the IP and applications layer. April–March fiscal year.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue to add new mobility consumers and extend our market leadership
- Continue transforming digital connectivity and digital services at home
- Expand and deepen our business customer base
- Monetise our platforms in overseas markets
